raw.details:
GLITCHED – Competitive Debugging Event

GLITCHED is a focused, multi-round competitive debugging event designed to test diagnostic speed, systems thinking, and practical fixability under time pressure. Organized by the Game Developers Association (GDA) CRCE.

Guidelines:

Team Size: Upto 3 members per team (the team members must be from the same year, branch, and division).

Eligibility: ONLY CRCE STUDENTS ARE ALLOWED.

Inter-college Team Members: NOT Allowed.

Number of Rounds & Problem Statements:

Round 1 (Qualification – Online Platform): Pseudo-code debugging involving multiple problem statements, game visuals, and pseudo-code.

Round 2 (Game Debugging): Project/game files containing functional bugs to locate and fix.

Final Round (Finals Challenge): A complex final project containing interconnected systems and cascading bugs.

Duration & Structure:

2 Days of competitive debugging (Day 1: Qualification Rounds 1 & 2; Day 2: Finals).

Elimination Flow: All registered teams → Round 1 (50% qualify) → Round 2 (6–8 teams or 30% qualify) → Final Challenge (1 Winner & 1 Runner-up, 1 FE Winner).

Special Provision for First-Year Students: Since first-year students have examinations, their Round 1 will be held at 12:00 PM. First-year teams will not have a Round 2. Teams that qualify from Round 1 will directly advance to the third and final round (Finals Challenge).

Rules & Regulations:

Fair Play: Teams must work exclusively on their assigned project/environment. Intentionally damaging, interfering with, or sabotaging another team’s project or system will lead to immediate disqualification.

Scope Control: Teams may modify only the specific files or components permitted by the organizers for each round.

AI & Internet Policy:

Round 1: Internet allowed, NO AI allowed. Teams must rely purely on problem statements and pseudo-code. No mobile phones or smart gadgets allowed.

Round 2 & Finals: AI is completely allowed strictly for navigating files, understanding codebase layout, and analyzing system architecture—NOT for actual code solving/fixing. Raw AI prompt outputs cannot be directly copy-pasted; manual integration is mandatory due to custom package setups.

Submissions & Deadlines:

All modifications, reports, and final patched project repositories with a clean git commit history must be submitted within the allotted time. Strict deadlines apply.

Final Deliverables:

Finalists must submit a patched project repository, clean git commit history, a one-page debugging report, and present a short demo with a live Q&A session with the judges.
